The past four days we have been asking questions about a whole table. Today we will learn to manipulate datasets to allow us to examine slices and subsets.

Day 5 is all about one pattern, and it is one that forms the basis for many, many data science analyses. It has a common name, [**split-apply-combine**](https://vita.had.co.nz/papers/plyr.pdf), which defines the steps necessary to break a table into groups, run a calculation on each group, and then summarize the results across each group. Almost every real question about data
turns out to be that shape: not "what is the average", but "what is the average **for each**". This approach is similar to the even more general `map-reduce` pattern of data analysis, where the `map` step corresponds to `split-apply`, and `reduce` takes the place of `combine`. Generally, `reduce` encompasses a larger range of more sophisticated analyses than `combine`, and the `map` phase is implicitly structured around parallel processing workflows. 

This afternoon you will address some questions the pattern cannot answer, and learn some older, slower tools
that can handle them.
